result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36522-L36622){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection( partition=None, max_iter=10, weighted=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Kernighan-Lin bisection](/assets/graphs/kernighan-lin-bisection.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two squares with a diagonal, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edges D to E and C to F. Left, the starting split you pass, A, B, E, F (teal) against C, D, G, H (violet), cuts 8 edges, in the accent color. Right, after swapping pairs of nodes the halves are A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, and only the two accent edges D to E and C to F are cut, a cut size of 2.0." width="100%"} The Kernighan-Lin heuristic (1970) improves a two-way split by swapping pairs of nodes between the halves whenever that reduces the number (or weight) of edges cut, keeping the halves the same size. It is the classic method for balanced graph bisection: dividing a circuit between two chips, a computation between two processors, or a network into two communities of equal size. Applied recursively, it partitions into more parts. Edge direction is ignored. Without `partition=`, the start is a random half; use `seed=` for reproducible results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [partition]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[list, list] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional starting split as two lists of nodes (IDs or labels) covering every node. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of improvement passes (default 10). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to minimize cut weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the starting half. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[set[int], set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The two halves as sets of node IDs (the first evolves from `partition[0]` when a partition is given). Their sizes differ by at most one, or keep the sizes of `partition`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or `partition` is not a split of all nodes. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pass tentatively moves, alternately from each side, the unlocked node with the largest gain (external minus internal weight), locks it and updates its neighbors' gains, then keeps the prefix of swaps with the largest total gain; passes repeat while they improve the cut. A pass costs $O(V^2)$ here. Follows NetworkX's `kernighan_lin_bisection`. NetworkX occasionally accepts a pass whose gain is zero up to rounding (which only exchanges the two sides) and then continues, so on some graphs the two end in different local optima. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two squares joined by two edges: the bisection cuts just those two edges: ::: {#b43eceeb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G"), ("G", "H"), ("H", "E"), ("E", "G"), ("D", "E"), ("C", "F")] ) left, right = g.kernighan_lin_bisection(partition=(["A", "B", "E", "F"], ["C", "D", "G", "H"])) sorted(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in left), g.cut_size(list(left)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], 2.0) ``` ::: :::
